ordering: Each block shuffles all 368 queries with its frozen seed. Rotate the first method by query index; reverse the base method order between blocks. Freeze exact block commands and schedules before competitive execution. Each block requests runner repeat=1.
input_contract: The original PNML and original single-property XML define the task. Startup, per-property staging or conversion, and all branches share one strict five-second whole-property invocation. No canonical-input shortcut or per-branch budget renewal. Benchmark acquisition and common integrity hashing occur before timing; each tool's query-specific preprocessing occurs within its deadline.

validation.native: Separate bounded independent original-input translation and witness/certificate checking
validation.competitors: Tool-reported unless separately and explicitly checked

acceptance: Accept a definitive result only with valid property semantics, complete agreed output, wall_seconds <= 5, exit_code=0, no timeout/deadline/memory/error/capability/subprocess failure, and successful bounded independent checking for native answers. Failed external definitive output becomes unknown before publication; preserve raw output, reported truth and every failure flag. A retained failed invocation is valid evidence of an unknown outcome, not an automatic campaign-audit failure. Any invalid accepted answer or definitive disagreement fails the audit and requires investigation.
launch_gate: Freeze candidate, competitors, dependencies, runner, inputs, commands and this protocol by hash. Require qualified ITS runtime and exact four-tool known-answer EF/AG harness checks, SMPT backend capability checks, verified native source/build provenance, and an idle measurement host. Root owns launch. Preparation does not launch competitive measurements.
isolation: One solver invocation or native checker at a time on the measurement host. No concurrent builds, tests, deployments or other benchmark work. CPU affinity does not imply exclusive host isolation; record host and workloads. Preserve interrupted or partial blocks; no replacement runs under this campaign identity.

reporting.coverage: For each block and method report every original slot and every ordered-branch representative, by source corpus, family and pooled. Report reachable/unreachable/unknown plus overlapping failure flags. Report solved intersection and union across blocks as descriptive repeatability, never as a measured portfolio.
reporting.pairs: Compare native-excess with each external method within each block. Preserve exact gain/loss query lists, stable gains/losses across both blocks, and any solved-set variation. Also report joint unresolved and method-exclusive sets.
reporting.timing: Report summed solver wall time, separately summed native validation time, actual recorded solver-plus-validation costs, and mean solver PAR-2 charging every unsolved row ten seconds. External totals contain no equivalent independent proof-checking cost; state that asymmetry.
reporting.conditional_timing: For each candidate/competitor pair and reporting view, select only queries solved by both methods in both blocks. Use per-query medians, then geometric mean competitor/candidate ratio. Show subset denominator and query list. Report candidate solver-only and solver-plus-validation ratios separately with checking asymmetry explicit.
reporting.resources: Retain raw systemd and perf artifacts. Report peak memory and counter availability over the full denominator. Separate full and multiplexed counters; missing or invalid values are never zero and never silently dropped from availability counts.
reporting.reproduction: Publish exact frozen source/binary/tool/runtime identities, input/manifest identities, protocol and execution plan, terminal receipts, artifact hashes, saved validator requests/responses, audit source and all result rows.

scope: Two Linux development repetitions of the current candidate and three qualified competitors at five seconds. The current Mac 363/368 comparison and earlier Linux candidates are separate evidence and cannot substitute for these rows. No held-out, novelty, broad solver-superiority or precise confidence-interval claim follows from this campaign.
holdout: Do not select, import, execute, inspect results from, or tune on any reserved evaluation family. Only the two listed development corpora enter this campaign.
qualification_limitations: The ITS native runtime can print a correct negative formula and fail to exit within five seconds, and can reject negative-coefficient products. Such trials must remain unknown. Runtime qualification requires correct accepted EF/AG true/false results on supported synthetic fixtures plus conservative rejection of documented unsupported, nonterminating and oversized cases. The exact four-tool harness preserves its original EF-2 fixture and permits only ITS to return a documented timeout/unknown there; all other fixture/method pairs must return the known answer. No competitive outcome informed this exception.
